title: Fennel and split pea dal with beetroot relish

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Everything is a plain whole ingredient: split peas, tinned tomatoes, vegetables, spices and oil.

supermarket.reason: Fennel, raw beetroot, yellow split peas and the rest are everyday items at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only one large pan and a grater, with simple simmering and grating.

works.reason: 1.2 litres of water to 250g split peas simmered for 50 minutes gives a proper dal for four, and the lemony beetroot relish lifts the gentle spicing.

honest_times.reason: 25 minutes covers chopping, the 10-minute soften and grating, and the 50 plus 10 minutes of simmering matches the 60 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, the names match their ids, and only water is added unlisted.

seasonal_feel.reason: Two bulbs of fennel, the seeds and the fronds make fennel the point, and the fresh raw beetroot and mint relish keeps it light enough for June.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear British English a beginner could follow.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling pulse and vegetable meal with greens and a fresh relish, the kind a family would happily eat again.
